subject: Request: Scheduled release delay — one-time credit to cover launch window
messages:
From: Sophie Barnes <sophie.barnes@acmecorp.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled release delay — request for launch window credit

Marissa —

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: engineering at Acme hit an unexpected blocker with our model integration (token streaming mismatch in staging) and we need to push the public launch from Aug 1 -> Aug 21. That slippage affects our paid pilot window with two enterprise customers and materially changes our go-live revenue profile.

Can Redwood provide a one-time launch-window credit or temporary rate accommodation to help us preserve the pilot economics while we fix the staging issue? We're not asking for an ongoing discount — just a short, usage-based credit to cover expected additional inference spend during the extended pilot (estimated ~ $18k over three weeks).

I've attached the revised roadmap excerpt and a short note from our PMs. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,
Sophie Barnes
Product Lead, Acme Corp
---
Attachments: Acme-Launch-Roadmap-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Barnes <sophie.barnes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled release delay — request for launch window credit

Sophie —

Appreciate the heads up and the roadmap PDF. Sorry to hear about the blocker. We typically handle these as one-off accommodations tied to clearly defined timelines and acceptance criteria. To move quickly, we need two things from your side:

- Confirmation of the adjusted pilot dates and the customer names affected (so we can map against the contract).
- A short estimate of incremental expected spend (you mentioned ~$18k — can you confirm).

Internally I'll loop in Sales Ops and Finance to size a provisional credit and run the request up for exec approval if it looks reasonable. Aditya and Laura — can you help quantify the impact and propose a conservative credit band we can offer while we get legal signoff? I'll draft a short credit letter for Sophie once ops confirms the band.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sophie confirms figures and impacted customers (today)
2) Sales Ops (Aditya/Laura) propose a recommended credit by EOD Wed
3) I escalate to Karthik for exec signoff if the ask exceeds $10k

Sophie — if you want to schedule a 20-minute call, happy to do that this afternoon.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled release delay — request for launch window credit

Team —

I reviewed Sophie's note and the attached roadmap. Based on Acme's ARR tier and strategic importance, here are two pragmatic options we can offer quickly:

Option A (conservative): One-time usage credit of $12,000 applied across next 90 days. This covers ~65% of their estimated incremental spend and keeps commercial precedent minimal.

Option B (aggressive, strategic): One-time usage credit of $20,000 applied as a line-item credit to invoices over 90 days + a 10% temporary rate reduction for the pilot customers for the extended 3-week window. This is appropriate if we prioritize retention and reference potential.

Notes:
- Both options require a short credit letter (legal) and a HubSpot note tying the credit to the August launch delay acceptance criteria.
- If we proceed with Option B, I recommend Sales Ops run a quick break-even to confirm we don't exceed acquisition allowances.

Aditya/Laura — please attach the quick credit matrix and the recommended option (A or B). If you recommend B, please include the projected net-new revenue retention impact.

If there's no objection from Legal/Sales Ops, I can greenlight Option A immediately. Option B needs an exec-level approval call (I can schedule).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, VP Sales
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Barnes <sophie.barnes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, contracts@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled release delay — request for launch window credit

Sophie —

Thanks for confirming the dates and the impacted pilot accounts on the call this morning. Per our internal review we've approved a one-time usage credit. Details below:

- Approved credit: $15,000 (applied as usage credits)
- Effective window: Applies to invoices generated for usage from Aug 1 -> Oct 1, 2028 (90 days)
- Conditions: Credit is contingent on (1) Acme confirming the updated public launch date in writing, and (2) affected pilot customers remaining under the current pilot agreements.

We've attached the credit approval letter and the credit matrix for your records. Legal has been CC'd (contracts@acmecorp.com) to run a short sign-off and will issue a countersigned letter. This is a one-time accommodation; future slips will be handled per standard commercial terms.

Next steps:
1) Sophie/Acme: Reply to confirm acceptance of the conditions and updated launch date (today).
2) Acme Legal: Sign countersigned credit letter (we'll route via DocuSign).
3) Sales Ops: Sean will apply the credit in the billing system once countersigned.

We appreciate your partnership and looking forward to the launch. If anything changes, loop us back in.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: credit-approval-letter-ACME.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB); credit-matrix-ACME.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12KB)
